(trouble) signifies in the New Testament a Roman province which included the whole of the Peloponnesus and the greater part of Hellas proper, with the adjacent islands. This province, with that of Macedonia, comprehended the while of Greece; hence Achaia and Macedonia are frequently mentioned together in the New Testament to indicate all Greece.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The faith, love, and patience of the Thessalonians, are evident tokens of their election which was manifested in the power with which the gospel came to them (vv. 1–5); Its powerful and exemplary effects upon their hearts and lives (vv. 6–10). People named: Paul, Silvanus, Timotheus. Places: Macedonia, Achaia.
ch.mh: As all good comes from God, so no good can be hoped for by sinners, but from God in Christ.

ch.aq: By this we may know our election, if we not only speak of the things of God with out lips, but feel their power in our hearts, mortifying our lusts, weaning us from the world, and raising us up to heavenly things.
